comment: I'm sure she is a philosopher of good quality, but she is not an amazing instructor. Not terrible by any means but focuses on strange areas while leaving other key figures in the early modern period entirely out. Lectures are not engaging at all and she is not the best public speaker.

Miriam has an interesting albeit boring teaching style. She will have 'class discussions' that are really just her going on tangents loosely related to the course material. She has an itinerary for each class she tries to follow, but ultimately ends up way off course. Gets clearly frustrated and bored when students aren't responding how she'd like.
Professor Miriam is very intelligible about philosophy, but they are complicated topics for an FYS. 2 page reflections every week and a final paper with 30pgs of reading a week.

Miriam is my favorite professor at the university. If you actually like philosophy, you'll like her. Grades are a pretty accurate reflection of the work you put in. She's incredibly intelligent and fascinating to talk to once you get into upper-level philosophy. She also genuinely cares about students and likes to make friends with them.

The class I took was her first year seminar, "meaning and value". Professor McCormick is a little awkward, but she genuinely likes talking to her students. The readings each week are not too much at all but you do have to read with care because the content can be confusing. She is very passionate about philosophy so you must be ready to think.

I have had Dr. McCormick for FYS 100 and PHIL 272. Her courses are well designed and the level of grading and required effort is average to slightly above average. Her lectures could be a bit clearer, and are somewhat dependent upon class participation. Always willing to help outside of class and very clear about her grading criteria.

Prof McCormick is a passionate teacher with a real interest in her subject. Contemporary Moral Issues is a really interesting class with good discussion on controversial topics. Prof McCormick is always down to meet and go over things you might not understand.

Dr. McCormick is very intelligent and specializes in some very complicated philosophical ideas. Unfortunately those ideas don't make for a good FYS topic, and class was slow. She is nice and tries her best to explain the concepts, but it proved hopeless. Class did pick up toward the end of the semester. Not an easy FYS by any measure.

Her lectures are vague and often run over the class time to the point where she never finishes the lectures. She tells you the first day of class that responses for daily readings are not required for the participation grade, but she does grade them. She gives no feedback on exams or papers that is constructive.
Loved her in the class! She is very knowledgable about all the material she covers and is able to have great discussions in class. I would recommend her as a teacher to everyone! Fun class too
I think Dr. McCormick is a fantastic professor. Her class was fun, she's a fair grader and an easy-going woman. I would recommend taking anything she offers

Awful. Instead of guiding students, her directionless lectures leave them confused and bored. Students who disagree with her are met with disdain. Plus she's a very critical grader, but her smattering of illegible comments makes it practically impossible to tell where you went wrong. I would advise other students to avoid her.
I strongly regret taking this class. The only reason to take this class is if you're a philosophy major and have to.

Three- quarters of the class slept or didn't show up every time. The discussions were not really discussions, more of her thinking out loud. Overall you will not learn anything other than what you read in the book.

Fairly intelligent professor, not a stand-out vis-a-vis her peers. She makes the challenging material understandable, and is available for help outside of the classroom.  You need to take this class for a major/minor, and it's not the end of the world (nor is it great) to take MWP with her.
Mc'D!
kewldood
Dr. McCormick assigns a manageable amount of reading and explains it very well.  You are required to write a few papers, but she is a fairly lenient grader.

Fun, interesting class. Mccormick is really good in this class; she gave us interesting readings and mixed it up with videos, presentations, etc. She was always willing to let everybody have a chance to say something and was very unbiased in her presentation of the material. very nice, makes the class pleasant. overall, good prof.

She has embarrased in front of her students for being hypocritically closed-minded. She tells students they are wrong even if their arguments are logically sound. She has preconceived conclusions that she expects her students to make. Study the thoughts brought up in class, but don't bring your own.
she will flat out tell you you are wrong for having a different opinion than her... very very frustrating.

If you click with Dr. McCormick, then you can really have a good experience in her classes.  If you obviously try hard and show her that you're working, your grades will reflect that.  I've learned a lot from her, but she's definitely not for everyone.
Loves teaching the subject, but is an unfair discussion moderator and makes the class boring. Truly unfortunate - it could be such an interesting class.
core was a nightmare because of her
she is boring and doesnt accept anyone's opinions but her own
She's not great, but not terrible either.  She is opinionated, but she'll definitely listen to you if you make a clear and strong argument for yourself.  You better be into philo when taking her.
Very pushy with her values, boring etc
